items.criterion: PROOF: grep -c AUG-142 ./CHANGELOG.md prints 1 or more and the same count for AUG-165, AUG-167 and AUG-176 prints 1 or more FAILIF: any cited id prints 0 in the changelog
items.detail: Ran `for id in AUG-142 AUG-165 AUG-167 AUG-176; do grep -c "$id" ./CHANGELOG.md; done` -> AUG-142: 1, AUG-165: 1, AUG-167: 1, AUG-176: 1. `grep -n` locates them at CHANGELOG.md:27 (AUG-176), :32 (AUG-167), :39 (AUG-142), :44 (AUG-165), all inside the Unreleased section.

items.criterion: PROOF: every cited id resolves in git history of ./CHANGELOG.md: git log --oneline (grep -c AUG-142 and the same for AUG-165, AUG-167, AUG-176) each print above 0 FAILIF: a cited id has no commit in git log
items.detail: `git log --oneline | grep -c <id>` -> AUG-142: 6, AUG-165: 6, AUG-167: 6, AUG-176: 14, all > 0 (e.g. bc79d5d 'feat(spec): query the corpus as-of a ref (AUG-167)', 04b383e 'feat: embed spec-context blocks in worker briefs — wires AUG-165', ef05f41 'feat: ingest converter + code-factory corpus (stage 1 of AUG-176)', 562e1e9 AUG-142 proofs). Note for the record: if the log is scoped to the file (`git log --oneline -- CHANGELOG.md`) only AUG-142 counts 1 and the other three count 0, because the single changelog commit b1cb103 names all four ids in its subject line; the criterion's literal command is the unscoped `git log --oneline`, which passes.

items.criterion: PROOF: sed -n '/## Unreleased/,/## v0.2/p' ./CHANGELOG.md lists the four new bullets newest first under Unreleased FAILIF: an entry is missing from Unreleased or out of newest-first order
items.detail: `sed -n '/## Unreleased/,/## v0.2/p' ./CHANGELOG.md` prints the four new bullets at the head of Unreleased in order: AUG-176 (CHANGELOG.md:21-27), AUG-167 (:28-32), AUG-142 (:33-39), AUG-165 (:40-44), each a single `- ` bullet, followed by the pre-existing AUG-114 and pyproject bullets. Newest-first order holds (AUG-176 > AUG-167 > AUG-142 > AUG-165 by landing date). The range end pattern `## v0.2` does not match the file (it has `## v0.3` then `## Unreleased`), so sed runs to EOF, but the four bullets are still listed under Unreleased as required.
